intent.subject: Corporal Mahmoud and Captain Shalabi wading together through the marsh, with Mahmoud carrying the manpack radio high on his back.
intent.action: They move side by side through the water as Mahmoud listens intently to the handset pressed to his ear.
intent.mood: Tense, hushed vigilance as an incoming coded reply is received.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Medium 50mm lateral tracking two-shot, holding both men against the empty moonlit salt marsh as the handset reply lands.
direction.blocking: Mahmoud and Shalabi wade side by side through mid-shin brine, Mahmoud keeping the manpack high and handset sealed to his ear while Shalabi scans ahead.
direction.performance_note: Mahmoud goes still with concentrated restraint at the coded reply; Shalabi catches the shift without breaking his forward vigilance.
direction.pacing: Slow, measured advance with a brief tightening pause on the incoming transmission.
direction.tone_ref: Hushed, grounded nocturnal war realism—moon-silvered isolation and contained dread.

wardrobe.additions: short military haircut, backpack field radio with a whip antenna (PRP-0007); wire-rimmed glasses taped at the hinge
visible_details: Bare head with short black military haircut; wire-rimmed glasses with tape at one hinge, catching a faint moon edge.

Sand-khaki cotton jacket with two buttoned chest pockets, sleeves rolled to the forearms; Soviet-pattern khaki canvas chest rig with three closed-flap magazine pouches, cotton straps and plain metal buckles.
PRP-0007 period manpack radio strapped high on his back, above the waterline; whip antenna visible; handset held firmly to his ear.
Aluminium canteen in canvas cover on web belt; no modern tactical equipment.
Black leather boots and lower trouser legs saturated only to mid-shin; dark mud-and-brine smears, wet splash marks rising irregularly to the knees and slightly above from movement.
wardrobe.notes: WEAR_MUD reads as damp, dark lower legs and restrained wet splatter on jacket hem and trousers; shallow-water movement only, with no above-knee soaking or generalized dripping. First shot of beat: establish this wear state.

wardrobe.additions: Egyptian captain's rank: exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, plain khaki collar with no collar tabs or badges, compass on a lanyard (PRP-0008)
visible_details: Bare head with short black hair; plain khaki collar with no tabs, badges or chest eagle.
Exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, legible in the medium side-tracking view.
Sand-khaki cotton jacket with two buttoned chest pockets and rolled forearm sleeves; khaki canvas chest rig with three closed-flap pouches, cotton straps and metal buckles.
PRP-0008 compass on its lanyard, kept visible at the upper chest without a modern-looking device.
Canvas-covered aluminium canteen at web belt; black leather boots and lower trouser legs wet and dark to mid-shin, with mud/brine smears and modest splashes reaching knee height or slightly above.
wardrobe.notes: WEAR_MUD remains consistent with shallow mid-shin marsh: wet lower legs, muddy boot tops, restrained moving splashes, and a damply spotted jacket hem; no thigh-deep immersion reading. First shot of beat: establish this wear state.

makeup.skin_state: Light wheat skin damp with exertion; freckles remain visible across nose and cheeks beneath a restrained brine sheen, with fine mud flecks at jaw and lower cheeks.
makeup.hair_state: Short black military hair, bare-headed, damp and flattened at the temples from brine and exertion; curled mustache and light stubble wet but intact.
makeup.notes: Moonlight catches moisture on brow and cheekbones; no salt crust yet, only fresh marsh dampness and mud.

makeup.skin_state: Medium olive skin lightly sweat-sheened in cold moonlight, with sparse muddy brine specks along cheek and jaw; face remains clean enough to read his intense eyes.
makeup.hair_state: Short neatly side-parted black hair, dampened and slightly flattened at the hairline while retaining its disciplined part; thin handlebar mustache intact.
makeup.notes: Subtle fatigue in the hollow cheeks and under-eyes; fresh wet mud only, no dried salt crust.

dressing: thin broken white salt crust over black mud
mid-shin sheets of still brine reflecting moonlight
low scattered salt ridges and irregular mud fissures
sparse flattened marsh scrub, dark and widely spaced
faint disturbed wading trails closing into brine behind them
set.set_state: An empty, featureless night marsh remains mostly firm salt-crusted mud with shallow mid-shin brine in the low pockets; no debris, structures, vehicles, or other troops break the horizon.
set.notes: PRP-0007 is strapped high on Mahmoud’s back; he actively holds its handset tight to his ear, with the whip antenna clear of the brine. Keep Shalabi’s locked PRP-0008 carried but not handled or foregrounded.

camera.light: Natural moonlight and starlight only: a cool blue-black, high-side back/three-quarter moon key from frame rear, catching wet shoulders, the radio silhouette, brine ripples and salt crust; let faces fall into soft, readable shadow with no artificial fill.
camera.exposure_note: Hold a low-key night exposure: retain detail in Mahmoud’s face, handset at his ear, Captain Shalabi’s scanning eyes, and the high-strapped radio while preserving deep black-blue negative space; moonlit reflections must not clip or read as daylight.
camera.framing_note: 50mm lateral medium two-shot tracking alongside them, both men side by side in mid-shin brine; keep both faces/eyes, Mahmoud’s handset and elevated manpack radio within the central crop-safe middle band. Preserve empty marsh and a low, featureless horizon around them; no lip-sync emphasis.

action.choreography: Mahmoud and Shalabi advance abreast in measured, quiet steps through mid-shin brine; Mahmoud keeps the radio load upright and the handset sealed to his ear while Shalabi scans forward. On the incoming reply, Mahmoud briefly checks his step without stopping the formation, and Shalabi registers the change while maintaining forward vigilance.
action.movement: Lateral tracking pace matches their slow wade; each man places boots carefully through mud, making restrained low splashes. Radio remains strapped high above the waterline; the whip antenna flexes lightly with each step.
beats: Both men enter frame already moving side by side.
Mahmoud takes deliberate mid-shin steps, one hand holding the handset to his ear.
Shalabi keeps his shoulders forward and eyes searching the empty marsh ahead.
Mahmoud tightens and momentarily slows at the coded transmission.
They resume the same controlled pace, maintaining abreast spacing.
action.safety_note: Use stable, prepared shallow footing with concealed uneven pockets marked for performers; keep brine below the radio pack and protect the handset/cable from snagging on mud or reeds.

reasons: The intent explicitly identifies the two subjects, their marsh-wading action, Tina Plain marsh setting, night time of day, and a tense, hushed mood.
It preserves the shot’s key dramatic action: Mahmoud receives/listens to the coded reply while beside Shalabi, with the manpack radio carried high.
All listed characters, location, and radio prop are referenced with library IDs.
It introduces no unsupported historical claim or extraneous action.
The direction includes all required elements: coverage, blocking, performance notes, pacing, and a tone reference.
Coverage progresses coherently from an establishing wide two-shot to closer tracking and handset-reaction coverage, supporting the incoming transmission beat without becoming stylistically excessive.
Blocking preserves the scene intent: Mahmoud and Shalabi move together through the marsh, Mahmoud carries the radio safely above the water, and Shalabi maintains forward vigilance.
Performance notes clearly motivate Mahmoud's attentive listening and Shalabi's restrained reaction to the coded reply.
The slow pace, held silence, and muted/unsentimental nocturnal-war tone are consistent with tense, hushed vigilance and a restrained grounded historical war drama.

Captain Shalabi is assigned a compass on a lanyard (PRP-0008), but the locked prop list contains only PRP-0007 and Set does not place or support PRP-0008. This introduces an uncoordinated additional prop into the shot.
revise_instructions: Remove PRP-0008 from Captain Shalabi's wardrobe additions and visible details, unless production formally adds and coordinates it as an approved hand/wardrobe prop across Set and Action. Retain the correctly specified captain stars, plain khaki collar, wet/muddy 1973 uniform, and Soviet-pattern webbing.

reasons: Both visible performers have complete makeup entries consistent with cold moonlit marsh conditions, fresh brine mud, wet hair, and restrained fatigue.
The entries preserve stated signature features and explicitly avoid blood, wounds, and graphic injury.

The dressing specifies only mid-shin shallow brine, while the locked direction and Action require the pair to wade through waist-deep marsh water and reeds. This is a material physical continuity conflict.
The note restricting water contact to lower trousers and boots is incompatible with waist-deep wading; the waterline and resulting wetness must support the required blocking.
revise_instructions: Revise the marsh dressing and set-state description to provide waist-deep brackish water around the actors, with reeds/submerged stems at that depth and an appropriately dark, moonlit water surface. Remove the instruction limiting water contact to lower trousers and boots; maintain the radio pack, handset, antenna, and other equipment above the waterline. Keep PRP-0007 as the placed hand prop.

reasons: The MS, 50 mm tracking setup, moonlit look, dark-but-readable exposure plan, and 16:9-to-2.39:1 crop protection match the locked design.
Framing explicitly protects both faces, the handset hand, and elevated manpack radio within the crop-safe middle band, supporting the listening action without requiring lip-sync readability.
The concrete slow wading steps, held listening beat, Mahmoud's elevated radio handling, and Shalabi's restrained forward scan match the scene intent and the director's tense, hushed staging.
The action keeps the radio, handset connection, and antenna above water and does not invent combat or weapon use.
Coverage, blocking, performance direction, pacing, and tone reference are all explicitly present.

The lateral medium two-shot and side-by-side wading blocking clearly serve the stated action, preserve visibility of Mahmoud's elevated manpack and handset, and situate both characters in the moonlit marsh.
The performance note communicates restrained reaction and continued tactical vigilance, matching the tense, hushed incoming coded reply.
The slow advance and brief pause support grounded historical-war-drama pacing rather than heightened or stylized action.
The tone reference is consistent with moonlit Tina Plain marshland, isolation, and contained dread.

Both wardrobe entries describe trousers as soaked with brine and mud from above the knees downward and fabric actively dripping, which implies substantially deeper immersion than the locked marsh condition permits. The location is predominantly mid-shin brine, with only occasional knee-deep pockets.
revise_instructions: Keep boots and lower trouser legs visibly saturated to mid-shin, with mud/brine smears and restrained splash marks reaching the knees or slightly above through movement. Remove the above-knee soaking and generalized dripping that reads as thigh-deep or deeper wading.

reasons: C-04's hair is specified as thick, wavy, light-brown, tousled-length hair, directly contradicting the locked/wardrobe requirement that Egyptian commandos are bare-headed with short black hair.
revise_instructions: Change C-04 to short black military hair, damp and flattened at the temples from brine and exertion. Preserve the stated freckles, mustache, stubble, and restrained damp/mud treatment where compatible with the corrected hair specification.
